actives.cautions: Start 2-3x/week; mild tingling at first is normal.
actives.name: Azelaic acid
actives.whatItDoes: Evens skin tone and fades dark marks while calming redness; well tolerated by most skin types.

actives.name: Salicylic acid (BHA)
actives.whatItDoes: Oil-soluble exfoliant that clears clogged pores and smooths rough texture from the inside out.

actives.cautions: 4-5% is enough for most people; layer under moisturizer.
actives.name: Niacinamide
actives.whatItDoes: Regulates oil production, strengthens the skin barrier, and visibly refines pores and tone.

actives.cautions: Very well tolerated; works in cleansers, serums, and creams.
actives.name: Panthenol (pro-vitamin B5)
actives.whatItDoes: Humectant and barrier supporter that hydrates and speeds up skin recovery after irritation.

actives.cautions: Always pair with strict sunscreen; can irritate if layered with strong acids.
actives.name: Kojic acid
actives.whatItDoes: Brightening agent that inhibits excess melanin — useful for tanning, sun spots, and post-inflammatory marks.

deTanProtocol.principle: Stop new melanin first, then fade existing tan. Strict sun protection is what prevents the tan from returning; brightening agents only work if UV exposure is controlled.
steps: Lock in strict daily sun protection (SPF 50+ PA++++, reapplication, hat) before expecting any fading.
Add kojic acid for hyperpigmentation and tan fading — effective and available over the counter in most regions.
Add azelaic acid for dark marks, uneven tone, and mild redness — pairs well with brightening routines.
Use salicylic acid if the skin is oily or acne-prone — clears congestion so brightening agents absorb better.
Expect visible fading in 6-12 weeks of consistent protection plus brightening care.
deTanProtocol.title: De-Tan Protocol

steps: Splash cold water or glide an ice cube wrapped in a thin cloth over the face for 30-60 seconds to calm morning puffiness.
Using a gua sha tool or your knuckles, sweep upward and outward along the jawline, cheekbones, and brow — light pressure, 5 minutes.
Finish with moisturizer to lock in hydration.
Do this in the morning only; results are temporary but visible for photos and the day ahead.
depuffRitual.title: Morning Depuff Ritual (Ice + Gua Sha)

hydration.note: Drink water steadily through the day rather than in large bursts. In hot climates or with heavy activity, total intake can reach around 4-5 liters, but this is not a flat rule — pair higher intake with electrolytes (a pinch of salt, coconut water, or an electrolyte mix) and let thirst and pale-yellow urine guide you. Overhydration without electrolytes is counterproductive.
hydration.title: Hydration

indianSkinContext.note: For Indian skin tones in high-UV environments: hyperpigmentation and tanning are the dominant concerns, so strict sun protection with SPF 50+ and PA++++ ratings matters more than any brightening product. Look for broad-spectrum protection and reapply — fading treatments fail without it. Product recommendations stay at the type level (e.g. vitamin C serum, kojic acid serum, gel moisturizer), which keeps them affordable and brand-neutral.
indianSkinContext.title: Indian Skin Context

steps: Gentle cleanser — mild, non-drying; wash for 30-60 seconds with lukewarm water.
Vitamin C serum 10-15% — 2-3 drops on clean, dry skin; pat gently and wait about a minute (antioxidant + brightening).
Lightweight moisturizer — a thin layer only if skin feels dry or tight after the serum.
Sunscreen SPF 50+ PA++++ — two finger-lengths, applied to face, ears, and neck. Reapply every 2-3 hours when outdoors or near windows; wear a cap or hat and sunglasses in midday sun.
morningRoutine.title: Morning Routine — Glow & De-Tan (oily/combination skin)

points: Walk 10,000 steps per day — circulation feeds the skin.
Cardio 3-5x/week for blood flow and stress reduction.
Strength training 4-5x/week for posture, testosterone support, and facial leanness.
Take a short walk after meals — it blunts blood-sugar spikes that aggravate breakouts.
movement.title: Movement for Skin & Face

steps: Gentle cleanser — thorough cleanse to remove sunscreen, sebum, and pollutants (double cleanse on sweaty or long outdoor days).
Retinol or retinal (over-the-counter) — a pea-sized amount on a completely dry face (cell renewal; fades pigmentation over time). Start 2x/week and build up slowly as skin tolerates.
Moisturizer — seal everything in; use a richer cream if skin feels tight.
nightRoutine.title: Night Routine — Repair & Renew

habits.caution: Gentle movement only; stop if you feel sharp pain.
habits.detail: Sit tall, pull your chin straight back to make a double chin, hold 5 seconds, repeat 10x. Strengthens deep neck muscles and improves head posture.
habits.name: Chin tucks

habits.caution: Keep the lower back against the wall; do not arch.
habits.detail: Stand with your back against a wall, arms in a W shape, and slide them up to a Y and back down. 2 sets of 10 daily for shoulder and upper-back posture.
habits.name: Wall angels

habits.caution: Avoid over-plucking; step back and check symmetry in natural light.
habits.detail: Clean up stray hairs below and between the brows with tweezers for a defined, intentional look. Less is more — keep the natural shape.
habits.name: Eyebrow shaping

habits.caution: Only for people who can already breathe comfortably through the nose. Do not use with a cold, congestion, sleep apnea, or any breathing condition — when in doubt, ask a doctor.
habits.detail: A small strip of porous tape over the lips at night encourages nasal breathing during sleep.
habits.name: Mouth tape for nasal breathing

habits.caution: Presented as a habit, not a promised outcome — no posture exercise reshapes bone in adults.
habits.detail: Rest the whole tongue flat against the roof of the mouth with lips closed and breathe through the nose. Treat it as a daily posture habit.
habits.name: Tongue posture exercises

points: Eat protein-rich meals daily — skin, hair, and nails are built from protein; under-eating protein shows on the face first.
Eat fiber-rich foods (vegetables, legumes, whole grains) — gut health is closely linked to skin clarity.
Eat fruits daily for antioxidants and vitamin C, which support collagen and brightening.
Include fermented foods (curd, yogurt, kimchi) for gut balance.
Cut back heavily on added sugar and ultra-processed snacks — sugar spikes are a common breakout trigger.
skinNutrition.title: Diet & Lifestyle for Skin

points: Sleep 7-9 hours per night — most under-eye darkness, dullness, and slow healing trace back to short sleep.
Finish your last meal 2-3 hours before bed.
Practice nasal breathing at night (keep lips closed, breathe through the nose); it improves sleep quality.
If sleep problems persist, discuss them with a doctor rather than self-treating.
sleepHygiene.title: Sleep Hygiene

supplements.caffeineNote: Keep caffeine moderate (no more than about 400mg/day from all sources) and avoid late-day caffeine if sleep suffers.
supplements.framing: These are commonly discussed general-wellness supplements. They are not treatments, and anyone considering them should discuss them with a doctor first — especially if pregnant, nursing, or on medication.

items.name: Magnesium glycinate
items.note: Commonly used to support sleep quality and muscle relaxation. Discuss with a doctor first.

items.name: Vitamin D3 + K2
items.note: Many people are deficient, especially with indoor lifestyles. Discuss testing and dosing with a doctor first.

items.name: Chelated zinc
items.note: Supports immune function and skin health. Discuss with a doctor first; excess zinc causes copper deficiency.

items.name: Omega-3 fish oil
items.note: Supports skin barrier and general inflammation balance. Discuss with a doctor first.

items.name: Collagen + vitamin C
items.note: Collagen peptides are best absorbed alongside vitamin C. Discuss with a doctor first.

supplements.title: Supplements (general wellness — discuss with a doctor first)

traditionalMask.method: Mix into a smooth paste, apply a thin layer to the face, leave for 10-15 minutes, then rinse with lukewarm water.
traditionalMask.name: Haldi-Besan-Curd Brightening Mask (optional traditional remedy)
traditionalMask.note: A traditional Indian brightening remedy; gentle for most skin. Patch-test first and skip if you have very sensitive or broken skin. Turmeric can temporarily tint very fair skin — rinse thoroughly.

rxReference.name: Tretinoin (topical retinoid)
rxReference.status: Prescription-only in India, the US, UK, and most regions.
rxReference.benefits: The most evidence-backed topical for acne, photoaging, fine lines, uneven tone and texture; the gold-standard retinoid in dermatology.
rxReference.doctorNeeded: YES — a dermatologist should assess the skin and set strength and frequency. Causes irritation, purging, and sun sensitivity at the start.

rxReference.name: Isotretinoin (oral retinoid)
rxReference.benefits: The most powerful acne treatment in existence — can permanently resolve severe, nodular, or treatment-resistant acne.
rxReference.doctorNeeded: YES, absolutely — requires blood tests, ongoing monitoring, and strict pregnancy prevention. Never taken casually.

rxReference.name: Hydrocortisone (topical anti-inflammatory)
rxReference.status: Low strengths available over the counter in many regions; higher strengths prescription-only.
rxReference.benefits: Calms inflammation, redness, and dermatitis flares quickly.
rxReference.doctorNeeded: For facial use, YES — prolonged use can thin facial skin. Short-term, guided use only.

rxReference.name: Bimatoprost (prostaglandin analog, lash growth)
rxReference.benefits: Longer, thicker, darker eyelashes (originally a glaucoma eye drop; lash growth was the discovered side effect).
rxReference.doctorNeeded: YES — an eye-area product with real risks such as iris pigmentation change and irritation. Never without medical supervision.

rxReference.name: Minoxidil (hair loss)
rxReference.status: Topical forms available over the counter in India and the US; the oral form is prescription-only.
rxReference.benefits: The most evidence-backed hair-regrowth treatment; also used off-label for beard and eyebrow density.
rxReference.doctorNeeded: Recommended — a dermatologist should confirm the cause of hair loss first, since not all hair loss responds to it.

appFramingLine: Prescription treatments exist for [concern] and can be very effective, but they need a dermatologist's supervision. What we help with is everything around them — the routine, the habits, the tracking.
